title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 48 (Variation of Shareholders’ Rights)

content.overview: Section 48 provides that where the share capital is divided into different classes, the rights attached to any class may be varied with the written consent of holders of not less than three-fourths of the issued shares of that class, or by a special resolution passed at a separate meeting of holders of that class, subject to the articles and the Act. Dissenting shareholders holding not less than ten per cent of the issued shares of that class may apply to the Tribunal to have the variation cancelled.
content.glance: Class rights may be varied by 3/4 consent or special resolution of the class; 10% dissenters may apply to the Tribunal to cancel the variation.
content.study: Where the share capital of a company is divided into different classes of shares, the rights attached to the shares of any class may be varied with the consent in writing of the holders of not less than three-fourths of the issued shares of that class or by means of a special resolution passed at a separate meeting of the holders of the issued shares of that class. The variation must not be prohibited by the terms of issue of the shares of that class. Where holders of not less than ten per cent of the issued shares of a class did not consent to or vote in favour of the resolution for variation, they may apply to the Tribunal to have the variation cancelled; the variation does not have effect unless and until confirmed by the Tribunal. Current-law framing: identify the class and proposed variation; test 3/4 consent or class special resolution; note dissenting 10% Tribunal route.

sections.heading: Variation Mechanism
sections.body: Class rights may be varied by written consent of holders of not less than three-fourths of the issued shares of that class, or by special resolution at a separate class meeting.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.body: Variation must not be prohibited by the terms of issue of the class shares; articles and Act still govern.

sections.heading: Dissenters’ Application
sections.body: Holders of not less than ten per cent of the issued shares of the class who did not consent or vote in favour may apply to the Tribunal to cancel the variation.

examples.title: Class special resolution
examples.body: Preference shareholders pass a special resolution at a separate meeting to alter preferential dividend rights. Section 48 is engaged; dissenters with ≥10% may apply to the Tribunal.

examples.title: Dissenters’ challenge
examples.body: Shareholders holding 12% of a class did not consent to a rights variation and apply to the Tribunal under s. 48 to cancel it.

hypotheticals.question: Is a simple majority of the class enough to vary class rights?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 48 requires written consent of not less than three-fourths of the issued shares of that class, or a special resolution at a separate class meeting.

distinctions.title: Variation of rights (s. 48) vs voting rights (s. 47)
distinctions.left: How class rights may be changed and challenged
distinctions.right: Who votes on resolutions in the ordinary course

misconceptions.trap: Any board resolution can vary class rights.
misconceptions.correction: Section 48 requires class consent (3/4) or class special resolution, with a Tribunal route for qualifying dissenters.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 48 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify class and proposed variation. II. Test 3/4 consent or class SR. III. Check terms of issue. IV. Note 10% dissenters’ Tribunal route. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Class; variation; consent/resolution compliance; dissenters’ standing; precise relief.
